summary: Fucosidosis is an ultra-rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency, leading to progressive neurodegeneration and multisystem involvement. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) has emerged as a potential disease-modifying therapy, particularly when performed early in the disease course. However, neuroradiological reversibility after HSCT remains insufficiently documented. We report a male infant diagnosed with Type 1 fucosidosis at 6 months of age based on enzymatic and genetic analyses. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) demonstrated characteristic abnormalities, including central tegmental tract involvement.

title: Amygdala neurofeedback as an adjunct to residential dialectical behavior therapy for borderline personality disorder: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
summary: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is characterized by affective instability and amygdala hyperreactivity. Although dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) reduces symptoms and amygdala-related abnormalities, many patients show only partial remission. Real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) amygdala neurofeedback (amy-NF) directly targets hyperactive limbic responses and has shown promise in uncontrolled trials. We examined whether amy-NF adds benefit to inpatient DBT. title: MRI and proton MR spectroscopy in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a comprehensive imaging review.
summary: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) remains a leading cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability. Although cranial ultrasound is widely used as a bedside screening tool, brain MRI has become central to diagnosis, injury pattern classification, timing estimation, and outcome prediction. Furthermore, proton MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) provides complementary metabolic biomarkers that enhance prognostication. This review focuses on MRI and 1H-MRS in neonatal encephalopathy due to hypoxic-ischemic injury, addressing both term and preterm infants. title: Postoperative DWI morphology and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
summary: To assess whether the association between postoperative diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery differs according to lesion morphology. title: Neurovascular coupling in simultaneous EEG-fNIRS studies: A scoping review of analytical frameworks and clinical applications.
summary: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) have been used across cognitive and physiological states and in diverse clinical populations. title: Decoding Spatial Attention in the Cocktail Party Problem Using Whole-head High-Density fNIRS.
summary: Spatial attention is critical for solving the cocktail party problem, a longstanding problem in neuroscience and artificial speech recognition. Here we demonstrate that, in an overt attention task, the attended spatial location can be decoded robustly from single trial hemodynamic responses, using a whole head high density fNIRS system. title: An Efficient Convolutional Neural Network Model for Classifying Positive Affective States from EEG Data Considering Sleep Condition.

title: Brain Abscess Caused by Bifidobacterium spp. in a Previously Healthy Adolescent: A Case Report.
summary: Brain abscesses in children are uncommon but serious conditions. summary: Sleep disturbances are common in functional neurological disorder (FND), with meta-analytic evidence confirming their high frequency. title: Language prediction in multimodal contexts: The contribution of iconic gestures to anticipatory sentence comprehension.
summary: Evidence shows listeners predict upcoming words, and iconic gestures in face-to-face dialogue often precede their spoken referents.
